extracted.intended_audience: research institutions and neuroscience faculty (research administrators, department chairs, and assistant/associate professors) interested in applying for Brain Research Foundation Seed Grants
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and eligibility rules for applying to the Brain Research Foundation Seed Grant program (institutional nomination, PI eligibility, scope, funding amount, and timeline). Intended for institutions invited by BRF to nominate a faculty member for a Letter of Intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional invitation / nomination requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If your institution did not receive an invitation directly from BRF via e-mail, then you are not eligible to apply. To be eligible for this $80,000 two-year grant program, your institution must receive an invitation from Brain Research Foundation to nominate one faculty member to submit a letter of intent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility depends on receiving a direct invitation from BRF. The invitation authorizes the institution to nominate one faculty member to submit a Letter of Intent (LOI).

rubrics_metrics.name: Nomination limit (one nominee per invited institution)
rubrics_metrics.description: Your institution must receive an invitation to nominate one faculty member to submit a letter of intent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program expects a single institutional nomination; institutions should determine internal processes to select their nominee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal Investigator (PI) rank and appointment
rubrics_metrics.description: The Principal Investigator (PI) must be a full-time assistant or associate professor working in the field of neuroscience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only full-time assistant or associate professors in neuroscience are eligible to be nominated as PI. Other ranks/appointments are not listed as eligible on this page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant purpose — start-up funding for new and innovative projects
rubrics_metrics.description: BRF’s Seed Grant Program provides start-up funds for new and innovative research projects that lead to future opportunities, collaboration, and scientific advancement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should be startup-style, novel, and positioned to generate future funding, collaborations, or scientific advances. The program emphasizes innovation and potential for follow-on impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of research funded (areas of the brain)
rubrics_metrics.description: We are committed to funding research into all areas of the brain, whether cognitive, neurodegenerative, related to learning and development or diseases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research across the breadth of neuroscience topics is eligible; applicants can propose projects in cognitive neuroscience, neurodegeneration, developmental neuroscience, disease-focused work, etc. Review examples of previously funded studies in the Seed Grants Archive to gauge fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award amount and duration
rubrics_metrics.description: This is an $80,000 two-year grant program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget and project plans should align with a total award of $80,000 distributed over two years; applicants should structure aims and timelines appropriate for seed/start-up funding at this scale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application timing — Letter of Intent (LOI) round date
rubrics_metrics.description: The 2026 Seed Grant Letter of Intent round will open on Thursday, August 28, 2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and institutions should prepare internal nomination processes and the PI’s LOI materials in advance of the announced LOI opening date. Check BRF guidelines for final deadlines and any subsequent submission steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to find full institutional eligibility and application guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: To learn more about institutional eligibility and our application guidelines, click below (2026 SEED GRANT GUIDELINES / INSTITUTIONAL ELEGIBILITY REQUIREMENTS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This page provides high-level eligibility; applicants must review the linked detailed guidelines for complete instructions, required materials, and any additional eligibility criteria or submission procedures.
